title: Why does a pencil look bent in water?
subject: Science

objective.text: Explain that light travels in straight paths in a uniform medium and can change direction at an angled boundary between air and water, making a straight pencil appear bent.

concepts.title: Light travels along straight paths
misconceptions: Light always follows a curved path.

variants.content: In a uniform medium, such as still air, light travels along a straight path.
Remember: a light ray is a way to draw the direction light travels. Its path is straight while the medium stays uniform.

concepts.title: Refraction at the water surface
misconceptions: The pencil physically bends when placed in water.

variants.content: Light from the submerged part of a pencil travels from water into air. At an angled boundary its direction changes. This refraction makes the straight pencil appear bent.
The pencil stays straight. Light changes direction on its way from water to air, so the pencil looks bent.

Imagine a toy cart crossing at an angle from a smooth surface onto a slower surface. One side reaches the new surface first, turning the cart. This is an analogy for a change of direction; light is not a cart.
1. Light leaves the submerged pencil. 2. It reaches the water-air boundary at an angle. 3. Its speed and direction change. 4. Your eyes receive this light and the pencil appears bent.
Observe a straight, unsharpened pencil partly immersed in water from the side.
items: One unsharpened pencil with no sharp point
A small amount of room-temperature water
steps: Ask an adult to help. Place the plastic cup on a stable table away from electrical equipment.
Add a small amount of water and rest the unsharpened pencil partly in the cup.
Look at the pencil from the side at an angle to the water surface. Compare the parts above and below the surface.
Lift the pencil out and check that it is still straight. Dry any spills with the towel.
variants.explainsWhy: Light from the underwater part changes direction as it crosses into air at an angle. The apparent bend is caused by refraction, not by a change in the pencil.

timeline.teacherSaid: In a uniform medium, light travels along a straight path.
The pencil remains straight. Light changes direction at the angled boundary between water and air, so the underwater part appears displaced.

questionBank.question: Why does the pencil look bent in water?
alternatePhrasings: Why does the pencil look broken?
What makes the underwater part look shifted?
questionBank.answer: The pencil is straight. Light changes direction as it passes from water to air at an angle, making the underwater part appear displaced.

questionBank.question: Does light travel straight before reaching the water surface?
alternatePhrasings: Is the light path straight in one medium?
questionBank.answer: Yes. In a uniform medium light travels along straight paths. Its direction can change at an angled boundary between different media.

quiz.prompt: How does light travel in a uniform medium?
quiz.explanation: Light travels along a straight path while the medium stays uniform.
quiz.misconception: Light always follows a curved path.

quiz.prompt: Why does the pencil appear bent at the water surface?
options: The water physically bends the pencil
Light changes direction at the angled water-air boundary
quiz.explanation: The pencil stays straight. Refraction changes the direction of light reaching your eyes.
quiz.misconception: The pencil physically bends when placed in water.
